title: Guardrails Before the Send Button: Letting AI Draft at Scale Safely
author: Juan Rodriguez
excerpt: An AI that drafts ten thousand emails will eventually draft a bad one. The pre-send gates that catch it before your list does.
content:
AI drafting at scale is a force multiplier with a failure mode: it produces fluent, confident, occasionally wrong text at the speed of your queue. The answer is not less automation - it is gates between generation and delivery.

Gate one: the rules that never bend

Hard checks that run on every draft: no broken personalization tokens, no links to domains you have not approved, no claims on your forbidden list, length within bounds, unsubscribe link present. These are code, not prompts - deterministic checks do not hallucinate.

Gate two: the model reviewing the model

A second pass where a model scores the draft against the brief: does it match the segment, the tone, the offer? Scoring catches the subtle failures - the draft that is grammatical but wrong for the audience. Low scorers route to a human or regenerate.

Gate three: human eyes where they matter

Not every send needs a human, but some do: new campaigns, new segments, anything above a volume threshold, anything the first two gates flagged. The human reviews a sample, not the stream - their job is calibration, not copy-paste approval.

The audit trail

Log what was drafted, what the gates said, and what actually sent. When something does go wrong - it will, once - the log turns a postmortem from archaeology into reading. Guardrails plus a trail is what makes AI sending a system instead of a gamble.
